description: Synthetic train number; not a live schedule identifier.
Synthetic service category used to choose the coach composition.
Number of coaches on each journey of this train.
Comma-separated departure weekdays used by the synthetic journey schedule.
Synthetic dataset station code; used consistently across routes/trains/journeys.
Synthetic railway-zone category for regional variety.
Scheduled synthetic arrival time at the stop.
Scheduled synthetic departure time at the stop.
Days after the journey departure date for this stop.
Synthetic cumulative distance; increases along each route.
Stable identifier for one scheduled synthetic trip.
Journey origin; matches the train route origin.
Journey destination; matches the train route destination.
SCHEDULED, COMPLETED, or CANCELLED; main dataset uses SCHEDULED.
Coach label such as B2 or C1.
Journey coach type derived from class code.
Number of seat/berth positions in the coach.
Stable seat identifier within the journey-specific coach model.
Denormalized coach number for application convenience.
Unique numeric seat position inside a coach.
LOWER, MIDDLE, UPPER, SIDE_LOWER, SIDE_UPPER, CHAIR, or EXECUTIVE.
Synthetic layout row/bay number for physical-distance modeling.
Synthetic booking creation date; always before the journey date.
Number of passenger rows that belong to this booking.
First passenger in the booking, used as synthetic primary contact reference.
INDIVIDUAL, FAMILY, FRIENDS, GROUP, or CAREGIVER_COMPANION.
Synthetic Indian-style name; not linked to a real passenger.
Synthetic gender value for demo variety; not an identity assertion.
Synthetic non-contact token such as demo_contact_000001.
Synthetic display name for the group.
Expected number of passenger rows linked to this group.
FAMILY, FRIENDS, COUPLE, CAREGIVER, or GROUP.
Whether the passenger group is intended to travel together.
Synthetic matching priority; HIGH or NORMAL.
Booking of the passenger assigned to the seat.
Seat position assigned to the passenger.
ACTIVE in the current synthetic state.
Desired berth/seat type used by the matching engine.
Optional coach preference, commonly the current coach when same-coach exchange is requested.
Explicit consent input; FALSE means the person must not be suggested.
Whether candidate exchanges must stay inside the current coach.
Whether candidate exchanges must stay within the same class.
Non-medical synthetic scenario note where useful.
Passenger whose target eligibility is represented.
Reason such as WILLING_TO_EXCHANGE, NOT_WILLING_TO_EXCHANGE, ALREADY_IN_PENDING_REQUEST, or ALREADY_CONFIRMED_SWAP.
Named test scenario category; not a generated matching decision.

description: Test expectation for the RailTogether matching workflow.
example: Detect the split group, consider only willing candidates, calculate compatibility, and allow an application-level exchange request without treating it as an official railway reservation change.
